correctness.rationale: For orthogonal Euclidean products of full-dimensional compact convex bodies K_i, boundary hypersurface measure disintegrates into pairwise (D−1)-a.e.-disjoint strata ∂K_i×∏_{j≠i}K_j with weight p_i=(S_i/V_i)/∑_j(S_j/V_j)>0. Thus ν=∑p_i(ν_i⊗μ_{-i}) and μ=⊗μ_i. Necessity: test any continuous convex g on coordinate i, f(x)=g(x_i); ν−μ integral equals p_i(ν_i−μ_i) integral. Sufficiency: each factor convex order dominates under conditional convex test and average with p_i. Iterated argument gives separately-convex k-point inequality. The factor example is also justified: in a centered centrally symmetric star body, X=Tρ(Ω)Ω with independent T, density d t^{d−1}, and Ω cone-direction distribution. Given X, select sign ε=± with P(ε=1|X)=(1+T)/2 so E[ερΩ|X]=X, and symmetry leaves the endpoint angular distribution the cone law. Balls and centrally symmetric polytopes with constant support height have cone law=surface law. Moment identity Eμ r²=d/(d+2)Eν r² yields exact sharp λ-strongly convex gap; cylinder disk radius1×[-2,2] has p=(4/5,1/5) and second-moment gap (4/5)(1/2)+(1/5)(8/3)=14/15, giving 7λ/15. Checked d_i=1 boundary counting convention and that nonorthogonal affine maps are excluded. Arithmetic checker only corroborates symbolic general proof.
